idiom_name: serde derive: unknown fields ignored for self-describing formats, #[serde(default)] fills absent fields
implementation_notes: Serde ignores unknown fields by default when deserialising self-describing formats such as JSON - the derive only asks for its own field names - so the classic reader becomes a struct that declares the consumed subset; #[serde(default)] (struct or field level, or default = "path") supplies the missing-field half from Default or from a function, and #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] is the deliberate opt-in to strictness. For payloads whose shape is genuinely unknown, read into serde_json::Value and navigate with get(...).and_then(Value::as_i64).unwrap_or(default); #[serde(flatten)] into a map preserves leftovers when round-trips matter.
pitfalls: #[serde(default)] makes every consumed field silently optional: a producer regression looks like valid data with defaults, so required fields should stay without defaults (or be validated after parsing).
deny_unknown_fields cannot be combined with flatten (documented serde restriction), so "strict plus preserved extras" is not expressible in one derive.
Absent and explicit null collapse into Option::None; when the difference matters use Option<Option<T>> or a custom deserializer, otherwise a null value silently becomes a default.
